Subject: Priory Health - encryption + residency clarifications

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. As promised, I'm summarizing the key items our security team needs clarified so we can move to procurement. The list below is prioritized; happy to join a technical deep-dive.

Top asks:
- In-transit: confirmation of TLS support (versions, cipher suites), and whether mutual TLS (mTLS) is available for hosted endpoints.
- At-rest: encryption algorithms used, envelope encryption approach, and per-tenant keying.
- Customer-managed keys: support matrix (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, CloudHSM, on-prem HSM), key import vs. key wrapping, and whether HSM-backed CMKs are supported.
- Key rotation: supported cadence, zero-downtime rewrap, and any restrictions for pinned model versions.
- Access controls and separation: who can access plaintext keys and unencrypted data; are there role-based controls and audit trails?
- Audit logs & retention: sample log fields, retention defaults, options for longer retention, and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM.
- Data residency & retention: does hosted Redwood store any customer content outside the selected region, and what are default retention windows for request/response data and telemetry?
- PII handling: redaction/pseudonymization options, and support for scoped processing (e.g., tokenization before send).

I've attached our initial questionnaire (priory-security-questionnaire.pdf) and would like to get a short written response so our legal/procurement folks have material to review. Ideally we get answers to the bolded items by next Tuesday (May 4).

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Winter
Security Lead, Priory Health

Sam — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Appreciated. I'm looping in Ben (SE/crypto) for the technical details and attaching a short PDF that outlines Redwood's high-level crypto options. Below are short answers to the bolded items; Ben will follow with a more detailed, auditable response and sample artifacts.

Short answers (high-level):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 supported; TLS1.3 preferred for hosted traffic. Cipher suites are modern AEAD ciphers. mTLS is available for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted API we can enable mTLS for enterprise accounts on request.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM envelope encryption by default; per-customer data keys wrapped by a root CMK.
- Customer-managed keys: Hosted: AWS KMS (customer-owned CMKs), Azure Key Vault (HSM-protected), and Google Cloud KMS supported for BYOK via key-wrapping; HSM-backed options (CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM) are supported for Dedicated and Private.
- Key rotation: Supported; we provide rewrap APIs and recommended rotation patterns. Rotation can be staged without downtime.

Next steps we propose:
1) Technical deep-dive with Ben to walk through Cloud/HSM options and sample audit logs (30–45 min).
2) Provide sanitized sample audit log & short runbook (Ben will attach) so your security team can confirm fields and redaction.
3) Procurement: Marissa will follow up on contracting/timing.

Attached: high-level-crypto-options.pdf

Couple of asks for the deep-dive prep:
- Any specific KMS vendor you prefer (AWS, Azure, GCP)?
- Do you need FIPS 140-2/3 attestation for the HSM-backed key?

Thanks — will keep this thread as the single source of truth.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — Ben here (SE, crypto). Following up with the technical specifics you asked for and attaching sanitized artifacts. TL;DR answers up front, then specifics. Happy to take these in a recorded deep-dive.

TL;DR:
- We never import raw customer key material for hosted BYOK; we support AWS KMS/Google KMS/Azure Key Vault where Redwood uses a wrap/unwrap pattern and the root CMK stays in your vault (no plaintext key import into Redwood). For HSM-backed CMKs (CloudHSM / Dedicated HSM) we support HSM-wrapped keys and CloudHSM-backed CMKs for Dedicated/Private.
- Default audit/usage log retention (hosted): 30 days. We can extend retention or stream logs to your S3/Cloud Storage or SIEM (CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, GCP Ops) for longer retention.
- We do not intentionally replicate inference payloads across regions. Global routing metadata can be used for failover but payload storage is region-scoped per account.

Details:
1) Hosted BYOK model:
- For AWS KMS: Redwood supports two flavors: (a) KMS-wrapped envelope keys where Redwood holds encrypted data keys and KMS handles unwrap; (b) customer grants Redwood the Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions on a customer-owned CMK — Redwood never extracts raw key material.
- For Azure: we support Azure Key Vault with HSM-protected keys and role-based access; Redwood performs wrap/unwrap via the vault.
- For GCP: Cloud KMS supported; similar wrap/unwrap semantics.
- On-prem / Private: we can integrate with on-prem HSMs (PKCS#11) and support HSM-backed key storage.

2) Key rotation & rewrap:
- Rotation is supported via our rewrap endpoint; process is zero-downtime when staged correctly. We provide guidance and can run a rotation assist.

3) Audit logs (attached: audit-log-sample.json) — sanitized sample fields:
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id (uuid)
- tenant_id (redacted)
- region
- endpoint
- model_id
- token_count
- outcome (success/failure)
- policy_evaluation (which routing/crypto policy applied)

Notes on PII: request/response payloads are NOT included in standard audit logs. Any fields that could contain identifiers are redacted in-hosted logs; we can provide a sanitized sample with PII replaced.

4) Retention & export:
- Default retention: 30 days for hosted audit logs and usage telemetry.
- Options: stream to customer-owned S3/GCS/Azure Blob for indefinite retention; or export to SIEM via push/forward.

5) Compliance & attestation:
- For HSM-backed keys we can support FIPS-backed HSMs (CloudHSM) and provide attestation artifacts. SOC2 reports may be shared under NDA; we have a SOC2 Type II report and can share with procurement/security once an NDA is in place.

Attachments: crypto-runbook.md (runbook excerpt), audit-log-sample.json (sanitized sample)

Happy to schedule the deep-dive. Proposed times: May 4 or May 5 (US business hours).

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
